title: The Licence and the Shared Name

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Licence and the Shared Name connects software freedom with responsibility for shared reputation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It follows how code, services, data, and models acquired different rights and obligations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book then proposes separating open technical rights from participation under a protected common name.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its central concern is reciprocity without letting a custodian become an unlimited owner.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers can examine this institutional proposal alongside the historical problems it tries to address.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Software permission can preserve access to code without preserving access to reputation or customers.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book follows that gap through the history and economics of open technology.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It also examines the different rights attached to AI data, code, models, and services.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: One licence cannot perform every legal and institutional function in that environment.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This historical account prepares the proposal about the shared name.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed compact keeps technical rights separate from voluntary participation under a common brand.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Using the official name would carry additional responsibilities under explicit rules.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Distinct instruments would govern the mark, contributions, economic arrangements, authority, and exit.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The custodian would have a limited mandate rather than unlimited ownership of the network's future.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These are institutional design proposals whose practicality and consequences still need testing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the history before evaluating the proposed compact.
